claim: Meta-analysis of 100+ papers plus own tests on 20 datasets and 14 models: CoT helps mainly on math and symbolic tasks; on MMLU it adds little unless the item has an equals sign.
authors: Sprague, Yin, Rodriguez, Jiang, Wadhwa, Singhal, Zhao, Ye, Mahowald, Durrett
title: To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
transfer: Format gate: use CoT only when the task needs symbolic or multi-step computation; otherwise short direct answer.

claim: Chain-of-thought can sharply reduce accuracy on tasks where deliberation also hurts humans; in 3 of 6 tasks models showed large drops, the others mixed.
authors: Liu, Geng, Wu, Sucholutsky, Lombrozo, Griffiths
title: Mind Your Step (by Step): Chain-of-Thought can Reduce Performance on Tasks where Thinking Makes Humans Worse
transfer: Do not force reasoning on perception-like, exception-rule or implicit-pattern tasks; add a direct-answer arm in the probe.

claim: Longer reasoning by large reasoning models can lower accuracy on built tasks (counting with distractors, spurious regression features, constraint-tracking deduction); Claude models grew more distracted.
authors: Gema et al. (14 authors, incl. Perez)
title: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
venue: arXiv preprint (earlier brief says TMLR; not confirmed)
transfer: Cap thinking length per task class; stop at first checked pass.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction (no external feedback) struggles on reasoning and sometimes makes performance worse.
quote: our research indicates that LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Revision step is ON only when a runnable check exists; otherwise OFF.

claim: Survey: no prior work shows successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs outside special tasks; it works with reliable external feedback; large-scale fine-tuning enables it.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
authors: Kamoi, Zhang, Zhang, Han, Zhang
title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
transfer: Route revision through program execution, tests or tool output only.

claim: Models fail at finding reasoning errors but fix them well when told the error location, across 5 reasoning tasks; so the bottleneck of self-correction is error detection, not repair.
authors: Tyen, Mansoor, Carbune, Chen, Mak
title: LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
transfer: Spend effort on locating the failing step with an external signal (a failing test line), then ask for a local fix.

claim: Repeated sampling raises SWE-bench Lite coverage from 15.9% (1 sample) to 56% (250 samples) with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct, but without an automatic verifier majority vote and reward models plateau beyond several hundred samples.
authors: Brown, Juravsky, Ehrlich, Clark, Le, Re, Mirhoseini
title: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
transfer: Sample many only when an executable check can pick the winner; selection is the bottleneck.

claim: Compute-optimal per-prompt allocation of test-time compute was more than 4x as efficient as best-of-N, and on problems where a smaller model has non-trivial success it can beat a 14x larger model in a FLOPs-matched test.
authors: Snell, Lee, Xu, Kumar
title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
transfer: Estimate difficulty with a cheap probe; allocate more samples or revisions only to hard items.

claim: Inference scaling study: a 7B model (Llemma) with a tree search algorithm beat a 34B model across all tested inference strategies on MATH; smaller models with better inference are Pareto-optimal.
authors: Wu, Sun, Li, Welleck, Yang
title: Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models
transfer: For small models, budget tokens into search plus verification, not a bigger model; applies where a scorer exists.

claim: Adaptive-Consistency cuts sample budget up to 7.9x with average accuracy drop under 0.1%, over 17 reasoning and code datasets and three LLMs.
quote: Adaptive-Consistency reduces sample budget by up to 7.9 times with an average accuracy drop of less than 0.1%.
authors: Aggarwal, Madaan, Yang, Mausam
title: Let's Sample Step by Step: Adaptive-Consistency for Efficient Reasoning and Coding with LLMs
transfer: Stop sampling when answers already agree; spend more only when they split. Caveat: agreement is weak when samples are correlated.

claim: Self-consistency gains over CoT include +17.9% on GSM8K (as listed on the abstract page).
authors: Wang, Wei, Schuurmans, Le, Chi, Narang, Chowdhery, Zhou
title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
transfer: Vote only on closed-answer tasks; gain was measured on older, weaker models and may be smaller now.

claim: Multi-agent debate protocols do not reliably beat other prompting strategies such as self-consistency, though some improve with tuning of agreement level.
quote: do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies
authors: Smit, Duckworth, Grinsztajn, Barrett, Pretorius
title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
transfer: Do not add debate-style roles for accuracy alone; use forced divergence only on open-ended tasks.

claim: Tree of Thoughts on Game of 24: GPT-4 CoT 4% solved, ToT 74%.
authors: Yao, Yu, Zhao, Shafran, Griffiths, Cao, Narasimhan
title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
transfer: Search over partial thoughts only where partial states can be scored cheaply and reliably.

claim: Reflexion reports 91% pass@1 on HumanEval versus 80% earlier for GPT-4; agents reflect on task feedback and store reflections in episodic memory. Feedback is external or simulated.
authors: Shinn, Cassano, Berman, Gopinath, Narasimhan, Yao
title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
transfer: Lesson memory written only after an external pass or fail signal. Base model and ablation tables not read.

claim: Self-Refine reports about 20% absolute average improvement using self-feedback, with the model judging itself; this conflicts with later findings that intrinsic feedback is unreliable on reasoning.
quote: improving by ~20% absolute on average in task performance
authors: Madaan, Tandon, Gupta, Hallinan, Gao, Wiegreffe, Alon, Dziri, Prabhumoye, Yang et al.
title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
transfer: Treat as valid for style and open-ended tasks where no ground truth exists; do not rely on it for single-answer reasoning.

claim: Process-supervised verifier solved 78% of a representative MATH test subset in reranking.
quote: Our process-supervised model solves 78% of problems from a representative subset of the MATH test set.
authors: Lightman, Kosaraju, Burda, Edwards, Baker, Lee, Leike, Schulman, Sutskever, Cobbe
title: Let's Verify Step by Step
transfer: Needs a trained verifier; transfer form is step-level program checks.

claim: Reasoning models show accuracy collapse past a complexity level; effort rises then falls even with budget left; standard LLMs beat reasoning models at low complexity, reasoning models win at medium, both fail at high (same-compute comparison).
authors: Shojaee, Mirzadeh, Alizadeh, Horton, Bengio, Farajtabar
title: The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity
transfer: Route easy items to short direct answers; reserve long thinking for medium difficulty. Methods of this paper have been contested; one data point.

claim: Reasoning models overthink easy problems, spending excess compute for little benefit; self-training can shorten reasoning while keeping accuracy on GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA, AIME.
authors: Chen, Xu, Liang, He, Pang, Yu et al.
title: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
transfer: Early stop on easy items; the shortening fix needs training, so use a prompt cap instead.

claim: CoT faithfulness: reliance on the written reasoning varies widely by task, and larger more capable models produce less faithful reasoning on most tasks tested.
authors: Lanham et al. (Anthropic, 30 authors)
title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
transfer: Do not treat the model's written reasoning as a log of what drove the answer; use outside checks, not self-explanation, as evidence.

claim: Reasoning models often do not verbalize hints they used: reveal rates often below 20% across 6 hint types.
quote: The reveal rate is often below 20%
authors: Chen, Benton, Radhakrishnan, Uesato, Denison, Schulman et al.
title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
transfer: A critique step that reads the model's own reasoning may miss the real cause of an error; prefer behavioral checks.

claim: Models with 3B parameters or fewer do not consistently benefit from long CoT or from distillation of strong reasoners; short simple chains fit better (fine-tuning study).
authors: Li, Yue, Xu, Jiang, Niu, Lin, Ramasubramanian, Poovendran
title: Small Models Struggle to Learn from Strong Reasoners
transfer: For small models, prefer short chains. About training, so indirect for prompting.

claim: Budget forcing on s1-32B (trained on 1,000 traces) raised AIME24 from 50% to 57%; the gain comes with fine-tuning, not prompting alone.
quote: We seek the simplest approach to achieve test-time scaling and strong reasoning performance.
authors: Muennighoff, Yang, Shi, Li, Fei-Fei, Hajishirzi, Zettlemoyer, Liang, Candes, Hashimoto
title: s1: Simple test-time scaling
transfer: Do not expect forced waiting to help a prompted model; allow extra thinking only up to a cap with a stop check.

claim: Plan-and-Solve prompting beats zero-shot CoT across all datasets tested (size of gain not extracted).
quote: our proposed zero-shot prompting consistently outperforms Zero-shot-CoT across all datasets by a large margin
authors: Wang, Xu, Lan, Hu, Lan, Lee, Lim
title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models
transfer: Cheap prompt variant for math-like items; test against plain at equal tokens on current models.

claim: LoCoMo: long-context LLMs and RAG improve memory over long conversations (up to 35 sessions, about 300 turns) but still lag human performance substantially.
authors: Maharana, Lee, Tulyakov, Bansal, Barbieri, Fang
title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
transfer: Agent memory needs retrieval tested against a full-context baseline; memory is not free gain.
